text.p: The Turkish lira firmed to 86,200 to the dollar on Monday from 86,250 at Friday's close due to the lower dollar/mark in thin trade.
The central bank adjusted its dollar rate for banks' compulsory currency transfers in line with dollar/mark movements in the international markets during the day.
The bank's rate closed at 86,150 lira, down from 86,300 Friday.
The cash shortage continued and the central bank lent a total of 31.5 trillion lira.
The central bank sold 17.3 trillion lira at today's three-day repo sale at an average of 74.4 percent. It also lent banks 14.2 trillion lira overnight money at 75 percent.

The overnight money rate closed at 75 percent after moving between 74-75 percent during the day. The average rate was 74.91 percent on Friday and the central bank had lent banks 28.7 trillion lira overnight cash.
In the T-bill market, yields firmed one to two points amid the cash shortage. Yields have gone up by a total of five to eight points in the last ten days.
The most active December 4 paper yield traded at 118.25 percent after Friday's 117.72 percent.
The Treasury announced it will auction 189-day T-bills on Tuesday.
